testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, what does it mean if you see no spray coming from other vehicles?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught under the vehicle.
The tires have absorbed all the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has formed. Drive slowly and carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle's engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights should come on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should go off right away. If they stay on, your vehicle has a problem.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, but only on the rear axle.
No, do not use them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, do not use them together.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure you do not mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: If your vehicle has power steering, what should you inspect?
questions.explanation: For vehicles with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Overloading your vehicle can affect all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Overloading can harm a vehicle's steering, braking, and speed control.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in an air-brake vehicle?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have one-way check valves between the air compressor and the first tank. This stops air from leaking out.

questions.question: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: When driving a placarded vehicle toward railroad tracks, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes on the tracks.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not look them in the eye or respond to their gestures. Never speed up to challenge them.

questions.question: If your truck has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: Check that the header board is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to contain the cargo.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded on a truck?
questions.explanation: The driver is always responsible for checking the cargo and making sure it is properly secured, even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for an ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To find out if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature gauge do?

options.text: Slowly rise to the normal operating range.
Jump quickly to the normal operating range.
Flash until it reaches the normal operating range.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to the normal operating range.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after you start the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should slowly rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: How can you tell if a truck's trailer ABS is not working when you start the engine?

options.text: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on.
All the rear lights on the trailer flash and then turn off.
The blue light near the driver's door turns on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after you start the engine, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of the road?

options.text: They usually do not have moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer than other parts of the road. These areas can stay icy and slippery even after ice has melted elsewhere on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to remove the vehicle from the tracks.
Walk down the tracks to look for an oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle right away and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency authorities for help.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and when it is snowing or raining, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle more easily.

questions.question: What is true about transporting livestock on a trailer?

options.text: A law enforcement officer must inspect it.
It can make the trailer harder to handle because the animals move around.
Only a registered farmer can do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make the trailer harder to handle because the animals move around.
questions.explanation: Livestock moves around and shifts its weight during transport. This movement can make the trailer unsafe to handle.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, they should be:
questions.explanation: When you check your wiper blades, make sure they are firmly attached and not damaged or stiff. Clean them if they are dirty.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the air leakage rate should not be more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, air should leak at no more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle has a problem and should not be driven.

questions.question: If you do not know the area where you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to get familiar with the area.
Do not use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Wait for someone else to back up so you can see how they do it.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to get familiar with the area.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you do not know the area, get out and walk around to see your path before you start backing up.

questions.question: To make it easier to leave a parked spot, you should park:

options.text: So you can back up when leaving.
So you can pull forward when leaving.
Only on the side of roads, not in parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous and should be avoided. Park in a space where you can pull forward when you leave.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: To avoid blocking traffic while driving a heavy vehicle, you should:

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while going uphill.
Ride the brakes while going downhill.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle cannot match the speed of traffic around you, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Be very careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal if spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, you should:

options.text: Only inspect the cargo if it is making noise.
Only inspect the cargo if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Trailers should:

options.text: Be overloaded to work more efficiently.
Not be overloaded because it is dangerous.
Not be overloaded because drivers are only paid for certain weights.
Have all weight loaded directly behind the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be overloaded because it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle is dangerous. It can damage the vehicle and make it hard to control.

questions.question: The minimum tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, you:

options.text: Do not need to wear a seat belt.
Must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
Must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must always wear a safety belt when driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.
One minute after hitting the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the area you can see. Slow down when visibility is poor.

questions.question: To avoid a crash, you should know that:

options.text: Braking is always the best choice.
Swerving may work better than braking.
Drivers should leave 100 yards between their vehicle and the next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice. You can usually turn to avoid an object faster than you can stop.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles that have this valve, a lever on the dashboard controls it.

questions.question: When you cannot see other vehicles clearly, such as at dawn or dusk, you should:
questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system use?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo
Protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo
questions.explanation: A header board protects a driver from cargo that moves during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Which statement about hydroplaning is true?

options.text: It usually happens when vehicles travel above 65 mph
It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You do not need much water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance becomes ____ times longer.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance becomes four times longer. A crash at double speed will also cause four times more impact.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, you may have a leak.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, a person must do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat test, complete a Federal Security Threat Assessment, prove U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, and have an FBI fingerprint check and federal background check done.

questions.question: After a trip, what should you do?

options.text: Take the vehicle out of service

questions.explanation: After a trip, you may need to inspect the vehicle and file a report.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you not do?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to avoid driving in fog. If you must drive in fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause a vehicle fire?
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by spilled fuel, under-inflated tires, electrical short circuits, smoking around fuel, improper fueling, loose fuel connections, or flammable cargo that is improperly sealed, loaded, or ventilated.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Fog makes driving very dangerous. Avoid it if possible. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: How much water on a road surface causes a vehicle to hydroplane?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. Even a small amount of water can cause this to happen.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, you will still have normal braking power.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then begin driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a dual air brake system vehicle, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Your CDL will be revoked if:

options.text: You want to add an endorsement.
Your privilege to drive your personal vehicle is revoked.
You have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your privilege to drive your personal vehicle is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your personal driving privilege is revoked, canceled, or suspended for moving traffic violations, you will lose your CDL. This does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: You must place emergency warning devices within ____ of stopping on the roadside.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the roadside, place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes. Turn on your four-way flashers when pulling off the road.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during vehicle inspection?

options.text: The driver may drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be put out of service until it is repaired.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is intact.
The driver must reduce the load weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be put out of service until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle must be put out of service until the spring is repaired.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.explanation: Curved convex mirrors on large vehicles are called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. They show a wider view than flat mirrors, but objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when turning, changing lanes, merging, and making other maneuvers.
